label: SRS with and without replacement — mastery test (unseen)

items.stem: In SRSWR, what happens after a unit is selected?
options: It is returned before the next draw
items.explanation: The selected unit is returned, so it can be selected again on a later draw.

items.stem: Which design permits the same population unit to appear more than once?
items.explanation: SRSWR returns each selected unit before the next draw, so repeats are possible.

items.stem: Under which design are successive draws independent?
items.explanation: With replacement, the population composition is restored before every draw.

items.stem: Which statement about the sample mean is correct?
options: It is biased under both designs
It is unbiased only under SRSWR
It is unbiased only under SRSWOR
It is unbiased under both designs
items.explanation: Each design gives the sample mean expectation equal to the finite-population mean.

items.stem: The sample proportion is the sample mean of:
items.explanation: Code each unit as one when it has the characteristic and zero otherwise. The average is the sample proportion.

items.stem: Under SRSWR, the variance of the sample mean is:
items.explanation: Independent draws each have variance σ²_N, so the variance of their average is σ²_N/n.

items.stem: Under SRSWOR, using S² with denominator N−1, V(ȳ) is:
items.explanation: The finite-population correction is 1−n/N when the population variance uses denominator N−1.

items.stem: Using σ²_N with denominator N, the SRSWOR variance is:
items.explanation: Since S²=Nσ²_N/(N−1), substitute into (1−n/N)S²/n to obtain the stated expression.

items.stem: A population has N=10 and sample size n=2. What is the FPC against σ²_N/n?
For N=5, n=2 and P=0.4, find V(p_WR).
For N=5, n=2 and P=0.4, find V(p_WOR).
items.check: Multiply the with-replacement variance 0.12 by the correction factor 3/4.

items.stem: If n=N under SRSWOR, the variance of the sample mean is:
items.explanation: A census observes all units, so the sample mean equals the population mean exactly.

items.stem: Which statements are true?
items.explanation: A, B and D are true. The sample mean is unbiased under both designs, SRSWR draws are independent, and for 1<n<N the SRSWOR variance is smaller under the same population-variance convention. Statement C is false because SRSWOR draws are dependent: each selected unit is removed before the next draw. At n=1, the finite-population correction equals one, so the two variances are equal.
statements: The sample mean is unbiased under both SRSWR and SRSWOR.
For 1<n<N, the SRSWOR variance is smaller than the SRSWR variance under the same population-variance convention.

A.why: The sample mean is unbiased under both SRSWR and SRSWOR.

C.why: Under SRSWOR, a selected unit is not returned, so the available population changes and successive draws are dependent.

D.why: When 1<n<N, the finite-population correction (N−n)/(N−1) is strictly below one, so the SRSWOR variance is smaller. At n=1, the variances are equal.

items.stem: A sample of size n is drawn from N units by SRSWOR. The probability of a particular unordered sample is:
items.explanation: All C(N,n) unordered samples are equally likely under SRSWOR.

items.stem: For N=20, n=5 and σ²_N=25, find V(ȳ_WR).
items.check: Divide the population variance by the sample size: 25/5.

items.stem: For N=20, n=5 and σ²_N=25, find V(ȳ_WOR).
Why are SRSWOR draws dependent?
options: The selected unit is not returned, changing the remaining pool
All units have unequal selection probability
items.explanation: After a unit is selected it is unavailable for later draws, so the next draw's possible outcomes depend on earlier selections.

items.stem: Which statements about unbiasedness and variance are correct?
items.explanation: A, B and D are true. Both sample proportions are unbiased, the SRSWOR variance includes the FPC, and a census has zero sampling variance. Statement C reverses the variance ordering.
statements: The sample proportion is unbiased under SRSWR.
The sample proportion is unbiased under SRSWOR.
For 0<n<N, SRSWR always has smaller variance than SRSWOR.
Under SRSWOR with n=N, the sampling variance is zero.

A.why: The sample proportion is unbiased under SRSWR.

B.why: The sample proportion is unbiased under SRSWOR.

C.why: For 0<n<N, SRSWR always has smaller variance than SRSWOR.

D.why: Under SRSWOR with n=N, the sampling variance is zero.

items.stem: For 1<n<N, the factor (N−n)/(N−1) is:
items.explanation: When 1<n<N, N−n<N−1, so the factor is strictly below one.

items.stem: Which variance convention pairs correctly with the formula?
options: Both population variances use denominator n
items.explanation: With S² defined using denominator N−1, the SRSWOR variance is (1−n/N)S²/n. The denominator convention matters.
